title: observability: token-level cost/latency logging + dashboards + alert tuning (v2)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Added token-level cost & latency metrics, new Grafana dashboard 'Token Cost/Latency v2', and tuned SRE alerts to reduce noise. Backwards-compatible: exporters emit additional metrics but old dashboards continue to work.
description: Context: We continue to see noisy SRE alerts around inference cost spikes that correlate to transient p99 token latency spikes and low KV cache hit ratios. This PR adds token-level cost and latency logging, extends tracing to include token-level spans (where feasible), wires new metrics into a unified Grafana dashboard, and tunes alert rules to use sustained windows and request-contexted thresholds. Motivation: reduce operational noise, make cost/latency regressions actionable by correlating traces, logs, and token-level metrics, and provide a single dashboard for product teams to diagnose performance/cost issues. Changes: 1) Metrics: expose new Prometheus metrics: redwood_inference_token_cost (per-request token cost in micros), redwood_inference_token_latency_ms{quantile="p50/p95/p99"}, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio (per-model,pool), redwood_kv_cache_latency_ms, redwood_inference_gpu_mem_bytes. Metrics are emitted with labels: model, revision, region, pool, tenant_id (when available). 2) Tracing/logging: add token-level spans for decode loop with span attributes: token_index, token_cost_estimate, kv_cache_hit (bool). Structured logs now include trace_id/span_id and request.id for correlation. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard 'Token Cost/Latency v2' with drilldowns: per-model cost/latency heatmap, KV cache hit analysis, and tenant-level cost breakdown. 4) Alerts: tuned existing alerts to avoid single-sample p99 noise. Key alert changes: - inference_token_latency_p95_sustained: fires when p95 > 1200ms for > 5m across >=5% of nodes - kv_cache_miss_surge: fires when kv_cache_hit_ratio drops by >20 percentage points vs 1h baseline sustained for 3m - token_cost_spike: uses increase(redwood_inference_token_cost[5m]) to detect cost regressions instead of absolute thresholds. 5) Backfills/migrations: added a lightweight Prometheus relabel rule to avoid cardinality explosion from tenant_id for high-cardinality tenants; high-card tenants are sampled to tenant_bucket label and documented in runbook. 6) Tests/docs: unit tests for metric instrumentation, local integration test using mini-runner to validate metrics emission, updated observability runbook and dashboard README. Rollout plan: gradual rollout behind feature flag (observability.token_level_v2) for 2 weeks, measure telemetry, then enable by default. Checklist: - [x] Implement metrics & traces - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and templating - [x] Add Prometheus rules and relabeling - [x] Add alert definitions and runbook links - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Run canary in staging for 48h Related: ENG-1423, PM-784, incident SUP-4321.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial instrumentation + metrics (add token metrics, labels), tracing + structured logs, Grafana dashboard JSON + templating, alert rule updates + runbook. Each commit scoped and tested locally.
files_changed: inference/metrics/token_metrics.go - new metric instrumentation and helpers
inference/tracing/token_spans.go - token-level span creation and attributes
telemetry/exporter/prometheus/relabel.yaml - relabel rule to bucket high-cardinality tenants
docs/observability/token_metrics.md - docs for developers explaining labels, costs, and backfill
Makefile - add target to validate dashboard json
observability/feature_flags.yaml - feature flag to gate rollout
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please avoid adding tenant_id at full cardinality; can we use deterministic bucketing for unknown/high-cardinality tenants?
Ava Martinez: Good catch — added relabel rule that maps high-cardinality tenant ids to tenant_bucket and documented sampling strategy in runbook.
Priya Desai: Alert thresholds look reasonable but suggest making p95 thresholds configurable per-pool. Also add a note in dashboard explaining threshold rationale.
Ava Martinez: Added pool-level variable to Grafana dashboard and made p95 thresholds per-pool via templating. Added explanatory panel in dashboard and runbook.
Marcus Lee: CI flaked on dashboard schema validation once; re-run and validated.
Marcus Lee: Approved after addressing relabel and dashboard templating comments.
notes: Staged rollout enabled via observability.token_level_v2. Monitor token_cost_spike alert for first 72h; if false positives occur, increase sustained window or switch to quantile-based scoring. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/token_cost_latency
discussion_snapshot: Final decision: use relabel sampling for tenants, per-pool thresholds, and 5m sustained windows for p95 alerts to reduce noise. Team will monitor for 2 weeks post-merge and follow up on ENG-1423 for further tuning.
manual_steps_after_merge:
1) Deploy prometheus relabel config to metrics cluster (rolling restart)
2) Apply new alerting rules in Alertmanager (dry-run in staging)
3) Enable feature flag for 10% of traffic, monitor dashboards/runbook for 48h, then ramp
4) Communicate changes to oncall and SRE via #observability Slack channel
risk_assessment: Low-medium: additional metrics increase cardinality risk — mitigated by relabeling and sampling. Alerts tuned to sustained windows to reduce risk of noisy pages.
